text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN

- The government has begun talks with a visiting delegation of an American concern, Southern Company, to decide the fate of 1,320 megawatt power station to be constructed at Keti Bunder, an official said.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif has formed a scrutiny committee to investigate matters pertaining to Sindh Accountability committees.
- Paramilitary troops were deployed in major Punjab cities on Sunday in a bid to halt sectarian violence that has left 45 people dead in August.
- The government has set up a crime watch committee which will facilitate close coordination between police, law enforcement agencies and the administration.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The state-run Pakistan Steel Mill has shelved its expansion programme because of an acute financial crisis.
- The new International Container Terminal at Port Qasim became operational on Sunday.

- The government is considering to grant the state-run Water and Power Development Authority an extra fund of 1.1 billion ($27.08 million) rupees for Ghazi Barotha Hydel Power Project already delayed by two years.
FINANCIAL POST

- Overseas Pakistani investors will be extended incentives similar to those given to local investors in preference over other foreign investors to buy public sector units being privatised, Petroleum Minister Chaudhry Nisar Ali Khan said.
THE MUSLIM

- On the third consecutive day of civil disobedience, activists of the Save Farmers Movement held demonstrations and blocked food supplies from some villages to main cities in Punjab province to protest against agriculture tax.
- The National Assembly (lower house) and Senate (upper house) have been summoned to meet on August 12.
THE NATION
- The leader of a Sunni militant group Maulana Azam Tariq has been arrested in a murder case.
THE NEWS
- The government will introduce a new bill in parliament on Tuesday to enable the higher judiciary to dispose of cases of terrorism and other heinous crimes within 30 days.
- Customs recovered 40 kg of heroin from a car and arrested a woman and two children near Azakhel in NWFP province.
- Army and police started joint patrols in parts of Rawalpindi city to check sectarian violence.
